title: Onset kinetics on a resolved neighbour cell: where a whole-cell threshold and a local one disagree
description:
A pre-registered pilot study. A published two-cell study (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23253738) solved the neighbour of a failing LG M50 cell twice with identical inputs, as a single temperature (lumped) and as a resolved three-dimensional field. This study integrates the B-CRNN decomposition kinetics of Koenig, Zhao and Deng (Chemical Engineering Journal 507 (2025) 160402) along its archived temperature histories: the posterior mean, passively (Stage 1, 49 cases) and with the reaction heat fed back one-way (Stage 2, five cases), and then 200 joint draws of the kinetic posterior and 30 Latin hypercube draws of the roll's published thermal properties (Stage 3). Conduction and radiation only between the cells; this is onset in a neighbour, not propagation. Each stage's predictions were public before its kinetics ran on an archived history (commits b09ef1d and 2657aee).

  • With copper busbars (500 mW/K in all) and 33.2 kJ, the resolved hottest node starts to self-heat at 0.15 K/min 23.4 s and 26.4 s before the lumped node (10 and 30 s releases); under the posterior-mean kinetics every start is a fresh SEI decomposing at 108.4 C.
  • Over 200 draws of the kinetic posterior the lumped node never starts before the hottest node, in any of the 42 two-strip cases; at 33.2 kJ, 30 s and 500 mW/K the lead runs from 15.4 to 58.9 s (2.5 to 97.5 %, median 26.3 s).
  • At that case, over the published spread of the roll's conductivity and heat capacity (contact, busbar and emissivity fixed), the hottest node's onset varies 0.027 times as much as over the kinetic posterior and the lumped node's 0.11 times (standard deviations): the kinetics set both onsets.
  • Scorecards: Stages 1 and 2, P1 to P4 held, P5(a) and P5(c) held, P5(b) failed; Stage 3, P1, P2 and P5 held, P3, P4 and P6 failed. Stage 3's check against the source paper's ARC test (V4) failed the brief's acceptance and passed only as amended after the failure.
